# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and a section's when the game first draws with its shaders, so
# that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's docs/porting.md,
# Prebuilt shader lists).
# Recorded by code, not by playing: bash tools/record_shaders.sh (its header says how) runs N64Recomp-browser's
# tools/record_shaders.mjs with tools/shader_plan.json, which loads the page fresh for each section. Section 0 is the
# launcher, the logos, the opening and the title with Start (Enter), and Mario Land on a new save. RulesBoard is A
# (Space) through Toad's greeting, the warp pipe and Rules Land into the board Toad teaches the rules on, then 90 s of A
# with four computer players on it. Then a section for each of the six boards, WesternLand to BowserLand, which the
# survey (patches/survey.c, tools/survey.js) sends Rules Land's trip to the rules' board to, with GwSystem's board index
# set as the game leaves for it, played by the computer for a whole turn: its start, four players' moves, the minigame
# it picks by its explanation screen, the results and back. Then the 60 minigames, six a section in their overlays'
# order: the survey takes the trip to the rules' board to the first one's explanation screen (0x5F or 0x60) with its ID,
# the groups the game's debug menu gives its kind (four players, 1 vs 3, 2 vs 2) and four computer players, as a board
# opens a minigame, each one's end to the next one's explanation, and the last one's to the minigame results (0x6F),
# which go back to Rules Land: the board's results (0x70), where some minigames end, read a board the trip
# never loaded. A plays them to their ends. Not recorded: the six duels, which pick among their board's spaces and so
# play only from a board's own duel, Mini-Game Land, the Mini-Game Coaster, a party's setup, a board's ending and the
# options. Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR, MSAA, upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means recording
# again.
